title: From one mutated cell to metastasis
caption: Cancer builds up over years as mutations accumulate in a single cell lineage. A benign tumour stays put; a malignant one invades. Beyond about 1–2 mm a tumour needs its own blood supply (angiogenesis), and metastasis, which causes most cancer deaths, sends cells to form secondary tumours.
alt: Five boxes in order: a mutated cell, a benign tumour, a malignant tumour, blood supply by angiogenesis, and metastasis.
description: A mutated cell: mutations accumulate in one lineage over years.
Benign tumour: grows slowly, enclosed, does not invade.
Malignant tumour: grows faster and invades surrounding tissue.
Blood supply: angiogenesis beyond about 1–2 mm.
Metastasis: cells enter blood or lymph and form secondary tumours.
